what_happened: The operator re-asked the disk-and-resume fix as a new request (20261028-091836-kbnb). The earlier retry chain had used up its $8 budget during planning, mostly on rounds that mechanical plan-rule findings consumed. A new request starts a new budget. The operator says the new request carries every correction, so planning should not repeat the loss. The event lists no unmet criteria, findings or failed checks.
cause: A job's budget is a single cap shared by every attempt and by planning. Nothing compares what is left against the stage caps the next attempt needs. Planning rounds are also not told apart: mechanical findings that a code check could settle cost the same as design findings. They use up rounds and money, so the budget can run out before any code is written. Once it is gone, the only way to continue is for the operator to re-ask the work as a new request.
prevention: Two code checks. (1) Before admission and before each retry, compare the job's remaining budget with the combined planning, producer and verifier caps. If it is too low, refuse the retry with a clear message, or ask for a decision to raise the budget. (2) Run the mechanical plan rules (the ones that can be checked by a script) on the plan before the critic's rounds start, and send the plan writer those findings in the same round. Mechanical findings then stop using up the critic's rounds, and the plan stage reports its spend so far.
proposed_request: Make Athena check a job's remaining budget before it starts a retry, and keep mechanical plan-rule findings from using up planning rounds. Outcome: (1) At admission and before every retry, Athena compares the job's remaining budget with the sum of the planning, producer and verifier stage caps. If it is lower, the retry is refused with a message that shows the remaining budget, the needed amount and the options (raise the budget or re-ask as a new request). (2) The plan rules that a script can check are run on each plan draft before the critic is called. The plan writer receives those findings straight away, and they do not count as a critic round. Acceptance: a test with a job whose remaining budget is below the combined caps shows the retry is refused with that message. A second test with a plan draft that breaks a mechanical rule shows the writer is told of it without a critic round being used. Replay the check against the budget records of job 20261028-055601-hg0n and the chain behind request 20261028-091836-kbnb to show what it would have said. Do not change the budget amounts in athena.toml.
